front.title: NeckLink Transport Protocol (NLTP): Loss-Healing Authenticated Telemetry and Reflex Transport for Constrained Networks

abstract.t: This document specifies the NeckLink Transport Protocol (NLTP), a lightweight, loss-healing, forward-secret transport protocol designed for microcontrollers, autonomous sensors, and edge gateways operating over lossy wireless links (including IEEE 802.11 vendor action frames such as ESP-NOW v1 and v2) and Carrier-Grade NAT (CGNAT) UDP paths. NLTP combines systematic Galois Field GF(2^8) algebraic Cauchy erasure coding with a single-round-trip (1-RTT) X25519 and pre-shared key (PSK) session handshake, ChaCha20-Poly1305 authenticated encryption with associated data (AEAD), a 512-packet sliding anti- replay window, optional pre-encryption zero-heap LZ4 block compression, integer delivery-rate pacing, and a confirmed out-of- line reflex channel that eliminates head-of-line (HOL) blocking for urgent actuator commands. The entire protocol executes with zero dynamic heap allocation and zero floating-point operations, fitting within 4,760 octets of static RAM in transmit-plus-reflex sensor configurations.
